subject: Operator access evidence request and sample artifacts for SOC2/SIG review
messages:
From: Elena Santiago <elena.santiago@greenpointhealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: security@greenpointhealth.com
Date: Mon, 11 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Access control evidence request for upcoming SIG review

Hi Jordan —

We are kicking off our vendor SIG intake for Redwood. The initial ask from our security team is focused on Access Control: specifically we need example SAML assertion payloads (including attributes used for group/role mapping), a recent SCIM delta (create/modify/deactivate) sample, and a role mapping export (CSV preferred) so our auditors can validate least-privilege practices.

Scope/questions:
- Can you provide sanitized samples (no PHI) showing a full user lifecycle (join -> role assignment -> role change -> deprovision)?
- Do you have a preferred format for the RBAC mapping (we can accept CSV or a small JSON)?
- Ideally we would like the artifacts by EOD next Tuesday (2025-08-18). Is that feasible?

Appreciate a single deliverable bundle and any short notes describing retention windows and how SCIM delta timestamps map to your audit logs.

Thanks,
Elena Santiago
Head of Security Ops
Greenpoint Health

Attachments: none

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Elena Santiago <elena.santiago@greenpointhealth.com>
Cc: irene.choi@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 11 Aug 2025 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Access control evidence request for upcoming SIG review

Elena —

Thanks for the clear list. We can deliver a sanitized evidence bundle that covers the user lifecycle and shows how SAML attributes map into our RBAC engine. Proposed deliverables:

1) SAML assertion sample (XML) with common attributes we map: eduPersonPrincipalName, mail, groups, role_claim
2) SCIM delta sample (JSON) showing add/modify/patch/deactivate events with timestamps and actor id
3) RBAC export (CSV) listing role id, role name, default permissions, and examples of role assignments to service accounts and users
4) A short notes doc (README) describing retention windows, log correlation keys (request_id), and how our audit log ties into the SCIM timestamps

Timeline: we can get a sanitized bundle ready by Tue 2025-08-18 EOD. Irene will prepare the SCIM delta and mapping notes; Marcus will produce the role export and a short description of our least-privilege review cadence.

One clarification: when you say "recent" SCIM delta, do you want a real-world 30-day slice or a representative synthetic sequence that includes every event type? We can do either.

I'll drop the bundle to a shared Drive link and send a JIRA ticket for tracking.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123]

Attachments: none

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Elena Santiago <elena.santiago@greenpointhealth.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 13 Aug 2025 08:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Access control evidence request for upcoming SIG review

Hi Elena + Jordan —

Looping in a couple of technical details so the artifact set is actionable for your auditors. Notes below and what we'll attach:

SAML assertion sample
- File: saml-assertion-example.xml (sanitized)
- Contains Subject, NameID, SubjectConfirmation, and AttributeStatement with attributes: mail, groups (comma-separated), role_claim, and external_id.
- Important: our role mapping uses the role_claim first, then groups as fallback. The README will show mapping precedence.

SCIM delta sample
- File: scim-delta-sample.json
- Format: array of events with fields: id, op (create/replace/patch/deactivate), timestamp (ISO8601Z), actor (admin|provisioner-service), and target.user.{id,email}
- For audit correlation we include request_id and trace_id in each event. Retention: SCIM change events are stored for 400 days; full audit logs with request traces retained 540 days (SOC2 scope).

RBAC export
- File: rbac-role-mapping.csv
- Columns: role_id, role_name, permission_set, default_assign_type (user/service), last_reviewed_by, last_reviewed_at
- We will include a few sample rows showing service account role isolation and a user-role change event referencing the SCIM delta id.

Redaction and PII: all samples will have emails replaced with user+hash@redwood-sanitized.local and no PHI. If Greenpoint requires original identifiers for deeper mapping, we can perform a controlled re-run under an NDA and coordinate redaction rules.

Delivery plan:
- I will upload the four files and a README to a secured Drive folder by 16:00 PT on Wed 2025-08-13. Jordan, please confirm if your team needs the files in a DocuSign-backed transfer or if Drive+JIRA is sufficient.

Regards,
Irene Choi
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com

Attachments (will be uploaded): saml-assertion-example.xml (application/xml), scim-delta-sample.json (application/json), rbac-role-mapping.csv (text/csv), access-change-timeline.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Elena Santiago <elena.santiago@greenpointhealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: security@greenpointhealth.com
Date: Wed, 13 Aug 2025 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Access control evidence request for upcoming SIG review

Thanks Jordan and Irene — this looks great and the timeline works for us. Drive + JIRA is fine for the initial review; we may ask for a DocuSign-backed transfer if our audit team needs signed chain-of-custody later.

Two quick asks before you upload:
1) Can the SCIM delta include one example where an admin-initiated role change was rolled back (showing both the original and rollback events)? That is a common check for our auditors.
2) Please include one row in the RBAC CSV that demonstrates separation of duty (e.g., role that cannot be assigned to the same person as a higher-privilege role).

If you can include both in the bundle we'll kick off the SIG intake and open a review ticket referencing JIRA-4456.

Best,
Elena
